anomalies.observed: On the 'FCC Peripherals' sheet the servo header PWLPOW1 is drawn with a 2-row symbol (Conn_02x08_Odd_Even). The eight even pins (2,4,…,16) each carry BOTH a '+5V' label and a 'GND' label on the same wire, i.e. the 5 V rail and ground are merged onto every servo power pin. The sheet's own note, however, describes the intended part as a 'Serva Connector (3 Rows, 8 Cols, 2.54mm Pitch)'.
anomalies.expected: A 3-row servo header in which signal, +5V and GND occupy separate pins/nets; +5V and GND must never share a net. The specification states '5 V feeds the servo/PWM connector bank (via PCA9685PW)', which requires a clean 5 V-to-servo rail, not a 5 V-to-GND short.

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals sheet: PWLPOW1 'Conn_02x08_Odd_Even', note 'Serva Connector (3 Rows, 8 Cols, 2.54mm Pitch)'; even pins 2,4,…,16 labelled both '+5V' and 'GND' on the same wire
5 V feeds the servo/PWM connector bank (via PCA9685PW)

anomalies.impact: Dead short of the 5 V rail to ground at every servo output. The MIC26903 buck would hit its current limit / shut down, no servo power would be available, and the board would not behave as intended (servos unpowered, possible regulator/damage).

parsed.summary: Most of the schematic matches the specification (correct rails, feedback divider, I2C/SWD/UART links, documented barometer pin-swap bug). The one deviation is the servo connector PWLPOW1: a 2-row symbol was used where the design calls for a 3-row header, so the +5V and GND net labels are placed on the same pins, shorting the 5 V rail to ground on the servo bank.
